question.problem:
$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t)=-2x(t)-y(t) \\ {y}^{′}(t)=4x(t)+2y(t)\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the system of linear differential equations above. The eigenvector corresponding to the only eigenvalue $\lambda =0$ of the system's matrix $A$ is $v=[-1,\text{ }2]^{T}.$ The vector $w=[0,\text{ }1]^{T}$ is such that $(A-\lambda I)w=v.$  Which of the following could represent the phase portrait of the system?

*Hint: Here, the dotted line represents the equilibrium solutions.*
question.worked_solution:
Since we have a repeated eigenvalue $\lambda =0$ (of multiplicity two) and only one corresponding eigenvector $v,$ the solution of the system is given by

$$
x(t)={c}_{1}v{e}^{\lambda t}+{c}_{2}(vt{e}^{\lambda t}+w{e}^{\lambda t}\,),
$$

where $w$ is a solution to the equation $(A-\lambda I)w=v.$

In our case,

$$
\lambda =0,\,v=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,w=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Thus, the general solution of the system is

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x(t) \\ y(t)\end{aligned}] & ={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}([\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]t+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]) \\  & ={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}-t \\ 2t+1\end{aligned}],\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.\end{aligned}
$$

First, notice that ${x}_{E}(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]$ are equilibrium solutions of the system since ${x}_{E}^{′}(t)=0.$ These solutions form the line with the equation $y=-2x$ in the phase space, as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14226345/assets/5c3afc4bedb411c778773190a3b9bc1db0b376dd69592ba744e8225ec900cc45.png)

Now, we consider some general solutions of the form

$$
[\begin{aligned}x(t) \\ y(t)\end{aligned}]={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}-t \\ 2t+1\end{aligned}].
$$

For example:

- When ${c}_{1}=1$ and ${c}_{2}=1,$ we get the following curve:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x=-t-1 \\ y=2t+3\end{aligned}
$$

Let's add it to the phase space:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14226345/assets/0d506993d3bfbb727dffd44ced1a588b40e2fefa86e7f2780d90277c9d0a9eed.png)

- When ${c}_{1}=-1$ and ${c}_{2}=-1,$ we get the following curve:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x=t+1 \\ y=-2t-3\end{aligned}
$$

Let's add it to the phase space:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14226345/assets/e88dfa02c57a5c31df14fdf6f963f7d568eaebccbbbfba6d8f2958593ac4693a.png)

The phase portrait of our system looks as follows:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14226345/assets/3f80cbae958772e0fa0492f5c426d412f002c3baa41a8a69b38e594512823422.png)
